raw.markdown:
# Rotator Cuff Repair Clinical Compass

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | RVU | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 29827 | Arthroscopy, shoulder, surgical; with rotator cuff repair | 23.18 | Primary repair code — full or partial thickness |
| 29826 | Arthroscopy, shoulder, surgical; decompression of subacromial space with partial acromioplasty | 8.42 | Often performed with repair; may be bundled |
| 29823 | Arthroscopy, shoulder, surgical; debridement, extensive | 7.12 | For irreparable tears or partial debridement |
| 29819 | Arthroscopy, shoulder, surgical; with removal of loose body or foreign body | 6.85 | If loose bodies present |
| 23412 | Repair of ruptured musculotendinous cuff (rotator cuff), chronic | 18.44 | Open repair — chronic tear |
| 23410 | Repair of ruptured musculotendinous cuff (rotator cuff), acute | 17.92 | Open repair — acute tear |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M75.100 | Unspecified rotator cuff syndrome, unspecified shoulder | Use when tear type not specified |
| M75.101 | Unspecified rotator cuff syndrome, right shoulder |  |
| M75.102 | Unspecified rotator cuff syndrome, left shoulder |  |
| M75.110 | Incomplete rotator cuff tear or rupture, not specified as traumatic | Partial thickness tear |
| M75.120 | Complete rotator cuff tear or rupture, not specified as traumatic | Full thickness tear |
| S46.011A | Strain of muscle(s) and tendon(s) of the rotator cuff of right shoulder, initial encounter | Acute traumatic tear |
| M75.50 | Bursitis of unspecified shoulder | Subacromial bursitis — may be co-billed |

## Payer Requirements

Tabs: Medicare | Medicaid | Private Insurance

### Medicare

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- MRI confirming rotator cuff tear (full or partial thickness)
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure: ≥6 weeks PT and NSAIDs
- Functional assessment documenting impairment (e.g., ASES, DASH, WORC scores)
- Physician attestation of medical necessity
- For acute tears: documentation of traumatic event and early surgical consultation

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Full-thickness tear with persistent pain and functional limitation despite conservative therapy
- Acute traumatic full-thickness tear in active patient
- Large or massive tear at risk of progression
- Partial-thickness tear >50% depth with failed conservative management

**Reimbursement:** Medicare reimburses arthroscopic rotator cuff repair under the ASC or HOPD fee schedule. Acromioplasty (29826) may be bundled with 29827 under CCI edits — verify modifier requirements.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare (CMS) | Covered with medical necessity documentation; CCI bundles 29826 with 29827 | Yes |

### Medicaid

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- State-specific prior authorization required in most states
- MRI confirming tear
- Documentation of ≥6 weeks conservative therapy failure
- Physician attestation of medical necessity
- Some states require peer-to-peer review for large/massive tears

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Full-thickness tear with significant functional impairment
- Acute traumatic tear
- Failed conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs, corticosteroid injection)

**Reimbursement:** Medicaid reimbursement varies significantly by state. Many states require prior authorization for all shoulder arthroscopy procedures. Rates are typically lower than Medicare.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicaid (state-specific) | Prior auth required in most states; rates vary | Yes |

### Private Insurance

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Prior authorization required by most commercial payers
- MRI report confirming rotator cuff tear with size and thickness characterization
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure: ≥6–12 weeks PT
- Functional outcome scores (ASES, DASH, or WORC)
- Operative report from prior procedures if revision
- Peer-to-peer review may be required for massive tears or revision surgery

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- Full-thickness tear with functional impairment and failed conservative therapy
- Acute traumatic tear in active patient
- Partial-thickness tear >50% depth with failed conservative management
- Large/massive tear with risk of irreparable progression

**Reimbursement:** Commercial payers typically cover arthroscopic rotator cuff repair with prior authorization. Bundling rules vary — verify CCI edits for 29826/29827 combination.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetna | Covered; requires MRI and 6-week PT failure documentation | Yes |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered with prior auth; functional scores required | Yes |
| BCBS (most plans) | Covered with prior auth; 6–12 weeks PT required | Yes |
| Cigna | Covered; requires MRI confirmation and PT failure | Yes |
| Humana | Covered with prior auth and medical necessity documentation | Yes |

## Required Documentation

**Imaging**
- MRI shoulder with tear characterization (size, thickness, retraction, muscle atrophy)
- X-rays (AP, axillary, outlet views) to rule out arthritis

**Clinical Documentation**
- H&P documenting symptom duration, mechanism (acute vs. chronic), and functional limitations
- Functional outcome scores (ASES, DASH, WORC, or PENN)
- Pain scores at multiple visits
- Documentation of dominant arm involvement

**Conservative Therapy**
- PT notes documenting ≥6 weeks of rotator cuff strengthening program
- NSAIDs trial documentation
- Subacromial corticosteroid injection record (if performed)

**Surgical Planning**
- Operative plan documenting approach (arthroscopic vs. open), repair technique, and anchors
- Anesthesia clearance if comorbidities present

## Submission Process

1. Obtain MRI confirming rotator cuff tear with radiologist report
2. Document conservative therapy failure (≥6 weeks PT, NSAIDs, and/or injection)
3. Complete functional outcome assessment (ASES or DASH score)
4. Submit prior authorization with CPT codes (29827 ± 29826), ICD-10 codes, and clinical documentation
5. Include MRI report, PT notes, and functional scores in submission
6. If denied, request peer-to-peer review with the payer's medical director
7. For acute traumatic tears, document urgency and request expedited review

## Common Denial Reasons

- ⚠ Insufficient conservative therapy documentation (most common — document ≥6 weeks PT explicitly)
- ⚠ MRI not confirming full-thickness tear (partial tears require >50% depth documentation)
- ⚠ Lack of functional outcome scores (ASES, DASH, or WORC required by many payers)
- ⚠ Acromioplasty (29826) bundled with repair (29827) — use modifier 59 if separately indicated
- ⚠ Missing peer-to-peer review for massive or irreparable tears
- ⚠ Incorrect ICD-10 code laterality (ensure right/left specified)
